reviews.text: If you have read any of my previous reviews then you will know that I am a massive fan of Early Access survival games, I have experienced so much asset flipping and ‘jank’ during my hundreds of hours playing survival titles that I am almost immune to being affected by it, and in some cases I can find it quite endearing, there is always an exception to any rule though and for me that exception is NeoJack Entertainment Inc’s latest title, Frontier Legends. Frontier Legends bills itself as an RPG action adventure where you can ‘live out your wild west fantasy in a world where survival, crafting and exploration shape your story’, this is roughly paraphrased and taken from the game’s description on its Steam store page, it is also one of the greatest works of fiction I have ever seen when it comes to a game, and that is being kind. The unashamed use of AI artwork on the games Steam page sent my ‘Spidey Sense’ into overdrive, but due to the overwhelming optimism I possess as a human (sarcasm very much intended) I was still pretty excited to jump into the game and see what it had to offer, this is a decision I very much regret. Booting up the game will give you a couple of choices, you can either join a multiplayer game hosted by another player (which is really not an option as there are currently only 2 people playing the game on Steam as of writing this) or decide to set up your own game and make this private, available to only who you invite or open it up to everyone. There are a few options available when setting up your game such as how long the day and night cycle will last, experience multipliers and other basic options that you have seen in other types of survival games. You are then treated to the character creation screen, and by treated, I mean the type of ‘treat’ where someone offers you a piece of chocolate but fails to tell you that it is actually chocolate filled with liquid human feces, not all surprises are good. The character creator has to be one of the worst I have ever seen, you want options? Diversity? Individuality? Then I am sorry sir, but you have the wrong game, you can choose to be male or female, choose a hairstyle from a paltry number of options, and also choose the colour of your hair, that’s it, this is gaming in 2026. The character models also look they have been designed by a special needs child that only had access to blunt crayons to express their artistic visions. So now that we have gotten all that out of the way, what can you expect when you jump into the world of Frontier Legends, not much really. I mean we were promised an adventure where survival, crafting and exploration would shape our story, sadly the reality is more like a visit to a badly maintained wild west theme park that was built back in the 80s, the type that as a child your parents took you to on your birthday because money was tight that year, don’t worry little Timmy, we will go to Disneyland next year, I promise! Frontier Legend’s world is as empty as it is ugly, and it is very, very empty. You load in at a generic station, in a generic wild west town packed full of assets purchased off the Unreal Engine store. There are a couple of NPCs nearby that will deal out your first quests that involve the usual uninspiring tasks that plague survival games, get some wood, make some axes, and then come back and talk to me, cool, this is something I can at least work with. So, I go away, I collect wood, I make some axes, I come back to the quest givers all proud and excited like the time I built my dad the worlds ugliest ashtray in woodworking class, and now the NPCs won’t talk to me anymore, much like my dad after he saw the ashtray. Must be a bug I think to myself, I will start a new game and try again, same result, broken, oh well let’s see what else we can do in this town. I spend an hour wandering around one of the blandest, soulless and empty places I have ever seen on Earth, it was like the set of a zombie apocalypse movie, oh did I forget to mention the game has zombies, they are the NPCs, they wander around doing nothing, saying nothing and are basically window dressing, I walked into the bank and various shops, took money out of the safe and cash registers and the NPCs just stood there and practically thanked me for doing so, I was expecting realism, I had obviously took a wrong turn somewhere on my map of expectations. The world is bland, the quests are bland, it is like cooking up Kraft Macaroni and Cheese and just not adding the cheese sachet. The animations and shooting mechanics are also laughable, to the point they are almost worth the price of admission alone, except for the fact that this hot pile of mess will set you back $41.95 AUD to actually play it, I am usually a pretty jovial fellow (sarcasm very much intended again) and would go easy on a game like this, but $41.95 for this early access, asset flipping, AI generated slop is pretty much a slap in the face to any self-respecting gamer, this isn’t even worthy of being called an alpha, it is more of a tech demo, I am just not quite sure what ‘tech’ they are trying to demonstrate. Steer well away from Frontier Legends, the dev has a history of releasing early access titles and abandoning them, they also do not handle criticism very well and will delete comments from people who offer valid criticism on their games, I was banned from the Steam community simply for trying to help out and offer up a few nuggets of wisdom on how they can improve their game, forget waiting for a sale, this one isn’t even worth a look if it was free.

Review Update 5/31/2026 I wanted to add a quick update to this review after getting more time in the game. I still want to give a positive review and do still think it is worth supporting at this point but I would caution considerably if you are buying and intend to play full out right now, I would wait. There are some pretty frustrating balance issues currently with player food and water requirements that make the game hard to really enjoy as is. I am honestly surprised this kind of base level balancing was not done during testing, especially after the demo feedback at least but it is what it is. Just because something is hard and frustrating that does not equal realism and I truly hope they get that and adjust those things. Also crop watering is very frustrating as you have to water them every few minutes it seems at times so that really needs to be address ASAP. So I do still stick by my review IF you want to buy this game to support the development and I am glad I have BUT if you are buying it now with the idea that you want to go hard and play it full time right now? I would really wait for a few patches without question. Initial Review: I was going to wait to review this game for a bit longer but felt like I wanted to at least get my initial thoughts and review after 4+ hours. This game is EARLY ACCESS and there is no doubt about that nor has anyone from the developers say otherwise so everyone should know what they are getting into when they buy it. Alot of the overly negative review seem very coordinated, which is a real shame. So far I have played a couple hours singleplayer and now a couple hours in private multiplayer with a friend and have enjoyed both very much. There are some rough edges for sure and that is to be expected but this is no asset, there has been alot of thought put into how things work and it will be a very deep and enjoyable game given some love and attention. Based on conversations with the Dev in Discord they are committed to this game and its future so I am very hopeful that the foundation that is already here will be built upon and it will end up as something really special. Again this is just an initial review and I will update it as the game and my gameplay progresses. For the price of a good lunch at McDonalds for two this game is well worth it already.

The Game: General overview. At its current state (day 1 release) there is roughly 5-10 hours of content depending on if you ignore certain aspects of the game. (town building). what you see now is the very foundation of the game. if you do not like early products with limited features this may not be the best time to jump in. there is a roadmap with planned content have a look and see at what point it makes sense for you. otherwise jump in and enjoy the ride, watch it grow. Character Clothing equipment to assist in survival, weapons, stat point distribution that affects character effectiveness. 3rd person and 1st person available (in game settings) Combat - ranged -- 3 pistols -- 1 rifle -- 1 bow - Melee -- hatchets -- pick axe Gun Play traditional cover and shoot, line of sight. Movement Linear, with some directional animation. Crafting mostly all tailored toward the town progression, with some personal items to assist in survival / gathering. Town Building Basic camps, various supporting structures, intro buildings to being hiring NPCs to gather resources. The Developers: the ones engaging the community in discord seem very enthused and open to disclose some information to the community, very responsive roadmap up in discord.

ok, so I'm going to get on a soap box for a minute. Last night I was so excited, I had a spare $25 and I wanted this game.. but lately I've been paying attention to reviews before I buy.. so I read the first 5 reviews.. all negative, all "don't waste your time or money", it's all assets, and a cash grab yada yada yada.. I took it to heart and bought 2 different games. What I should have done was waited until some trusted game reviewers released video's. Like GameEdged and KAGE848. Let me tell you what I didn't see. I didn't see a lot of assets that weren't refreshed, and made a part of this world. I didn't see a lot of hang ups, or jerky play. What I saw was a game that could have been Wild West Dynasty. What I'm seeing is a game set up like Medieval or Sengoku Dynasty.. What I see, is a great Wild West survival/craft/build game that I'm going to thoroughly enjoy. Should you buy this game? If what I described is your bag, then go for it. If it's not, then yes, don't waste your time or money. But if you truly enjoy Dynasty style games, this IS the game for you. Instead being medieval, feudal, secret island bases, or stranded on an island after a plane crash (how many times have we seen that?), it's in the early American Wild West... It's a survival build game.. it's not Fortnite, or PUBG.. it's a really decent game that I am and will thoroughly enjoy. Before you decide though, do yourself, and these devs a favor.. Go and watch videos of reliable player/reviewers, and see that the game is truly like. ok, off my soap box now.. I got a farm to build!! :-D

Great game! I watched some gameplay videos around its release and after and decided to buy it after a few patches. The game has a promising roadmap, and I like the direction it's heading in. The game definitely needs some performance optimization. At 4K with maxed-out settings and DLSS set to Quality, I get around 60 FPS, with drops to 50 FPS. However, I'm sure this will improve over time, or Frame Generation may be added. An x2 Frame Generation option would solve the issue quickly for the time being. The game lets you host your own server, which is a big plus for me and another reason why I wanted to support it. I'll give this game a positive review and keep an eye on future updates. I'm happy with the way things are progressing. The dev are active, and the Discord community is welcoming. I hope to see more players around!

Frontier Legends has a great foundation on paper—combining a Wild West setting with modular base-building, survival crafting, and cooperative town management. However, in its current Early Access state, the execution still needs a lot of polish to hit its full potential. Pros: The shift to a modular building system shows a lot of promise for player creativity. The environment successfully captures that rugged, open Wild West atmosphere. Cons: High Interface Friction: The newly overhauled UI and resource gathering loops still feel a bit clunky and tedious to navigate. Optimization Hurdles: The game currently suffers from noticeable framerate dips and technical rough edges that pull you out of the survival immersion. Under-baked Progression: Combat, AI behavior, and settlement management elements need deeper tuning to make the gameplay loop feel fully rewarding. Open, constructive criticism is the path to betterment. This project has a solid concept, but it needs a few more updates before it is fully ready for a smooth experience. For a complete, visual look at the gameplay mechanics and performance under the hood, check out my full video breakdown here: https://youtu.be/V7ID_mFMFFs

The first trailer on this page is what the game inspires to be, they second trailer is basically what you get. It talks about doing this and that, building a town, a legacy, but instead its a plot with basic looking work huts. It's basically a dynasty game, you know the ones I'm talking about. It's very meh in it's current state. It's playable, but almost nothing there. As with all those types of games they take a lot of time to get to somewhere you find a playable experience. If you buy it now, I don't know if the updates will bring you back. I feel the negative comments are a little harsh. It's EA. You risk your money with all EA games in the hope they can benefit from it to carry on working on it. AI is trash. They don't need to be looking at you to hit you. Shot a rifle man in the back and he hit me before turning to see me, that's how bad they are. Everything is way over healthed. What I don't like and I find it lazy when it comes to these games, all the others, medieval dynasty, Bellwright, they require you to build rep and find people suited to those skills. In this, you build a logging hut and hire someone from it and pay them a daily fee to work. Graphically it's okay. Nothing amazing. Villagers don't really do anything, just stand there and there's no way as many as those in the video. There are none out of town unless it's by a tent. It's just too early. I'll continue to play it if I haven't anything else to play, but it needs work.
